title: Finance Playbook: Budgeting, Procurement, Contracts, Revenue Recognition & Billing (Operational Playbook)
author: Priya Nair
content:
Overview

This operational playbook consolidates Redwood Inference's finance and legal core procedures for annual budgeting and forecasting, vendor procurement and purchase order (PO) processing, contracts and legal review lifecycle, and revenue recognition & billing policies. Intended audience: finance team, legal, procurement, FP&A partners, product and engineering managers who request spend, and revenue ops.

Scope & applicability

- Applies to all legal entities and product lines managed by Redwood Inference unless a customer or partner contract explicitly supersedes internal policy.
- Covers: annual budget process, quarterly rolling forecasts, vendor procurement and contract intake, PO approvals and issuance, contract review & execution, invoicing, collections, and revenue recognition guidance aligned to ASC 606 principles.

High-level process map (simplified)

1) Budgeting & forecast cadence: target budgets -> leadership review -> finance consolidation -> exec approval -> distributed allocations -> monthly/quarterly reforecasts.
2) Procurement & contracts: request -> sourcing & negotiation -> legal review -> approvals -> PO issuance / signature -> receipt / vendor onboarding.
3) Revenue & billing: contract intake -> billing terms captured -> invoicing schedule -> revenue recognition -> collections & dispute resolution.

Roles & ownership

- Finance (Owner): overall budgeting, revenue recognition policy, month-end close, forecast consolidation, billing operations. Primary contacts: priya.nair@redwood.example, daniel.morales@redwood.example
- Legal (Reviewer): contract terms, risk exceptions, signature authority validation. Primary contacts: emily.zhao@redwood.example, karen.oneill@redwood.example
- Procurement / Vendor Ops: vendor onboarding, PO issuance, vendor master data. Primary contact: vendor-ops@redwood.example
- Requesting Team (Requester): submits procurement and contract requests, provides business justification and technical acceptance criteria.

Budgeting & forecasting (detailed)

Purpose: allocate resources to product, engineering, go-to-market, and G&A while maintaining runway targets and growth investments.

Annual budget process (timeline, owners, deliverables)
- June - July: Budget kickoff and assumption setting (Finance, FP&A).
- July - August: Department-level submissions (Managers & Finance partners).
- September: Consolidation and executive review (Finance lead + Exec).
- October 1: Final budget approval and published allocations.

Forecasting cadence
- Monthly operational forecast (rolling 12 months) owned by Finance and department leads.
- Quarterly reforecast aligned to product roadmap milestones and sales bookings.

Key inputs & templates
- Revenue build (bookings, ARR, one-time services).
- Cost build (headcount FTE plans, variable infra spend, third-party model inference costs).
- CapEx requests (GPU purchases, hardware refresh).
- Budget template: CSV/XLS template stored in Finance templates space (link: /confluence/finance-and-legal/templates/budget-template-2026).

Approval thresholds (examples)
- Up to $5k: Manager approval.
- $5k - $25k: Director approval + Finance notification.
- $25k - $250k: VP approval + Finance & Procurement review.
- > $250k: CFO approval + Legal & Procurement review.

Procurement procedures

Purchase request workflow
1. Submit Purchase Request (PR) via procurement portal with business justification and budget code.
2. Procurement evaluates sourcing options; if new vendor, perform vendor risk checks and AML/KYC as required.
3. Legal review required for contracts or > $25k commitments.
4. Finance validates available budget.
5. PO issued by Procurement; requester receives PO and confirms order.

Vendor selection and onboarding
- Preferred vendors: use established master vendor list; see vendor-ops page.
- New vendor onboarding requires: W-9 (or equivalent), bank details, remittance instructions, vendor compliance questionnaire, and insurance certificate if required.

Emergency procurement (expedited purchases)
- Emergency purchases must be documented with business owner justification and require post-facto review by Procurement and Finance within 5 business days.

PO & payment SLA targets
- PO issuance for standard requests: within 3 business days after approvals for <$25k.
- Complex or negotiated contracts (> $100k): PO/signature within 10 business days after final approvals.
- Invoice payment terms: follow contract terms (Net 30 default). Early pay discounts must be approved by Finance.

Contracts & legal process

Contract intake checklist (Requester responsibilities)
- Provide signed SOW or proposal, commercial terms, contact information, and billing instructions.
- Provide intended start and end dates, renewal terms, and any subcontracting details.

Legal review & redline process
1. Submit contract request to Legal with intake form and draft agreement.
2. Legal triages risk: standard, negotiated, or high-risk. High-risk (data residency, indemnities, export controls, > $250k) escalates to General Counsel.
3. Legal returns redline and recommended fallback positions.
4. Commercial owner negotiates; legal performs final review of materially changed terms.
5. Signature: signatories must follow Signature Authority Matrix (see below).

Signature Authority Matrix (summary)
- Manager level: non-binding NDAs and low-value SOWs up to $10k (with Finance notification).
- Director: contracts up to $100k (with Legal & Finance review).
- CFO / CEO: contracts > $100k or with material legal risk.

Contract retention & storage
- Executed contracts must be uploaded to Contract Repository (DocStore) within 2 business days of signature and assigned a contract ID.
- Metadata required: counterparty name, start/end dates, billing terms, renewal notice period, data residency classification.

Revenue recognition & billing policies (summary)

Principles: Redwood follows ASC 606-aligned approach: identify contract(s), identify performance obligations, determine transaction price, allocate price to obligations, recognize revenue when control transfers. Billing and revenue tasks are coordinated between Legal, Finance, and Sales Ops.

Billing terms & invoicing cadence
- Default billing term: Net 30 from invoice date unless negotiated otherwise.
- Subscription/ARR: monthly or annual invoicing per contract; recognize revenue ratably over the subscription term.
- Professional services / one-time fees: recognized when the performance obligation is satisfied (completion of milestone or delivery).

Deferred revenue handling
- Payments received in advance are recorded to Deferred Revenue liability on receipt and recognized monthly over the service period.
- Refunds or customer credits reduce deferred revenue; impacts must be documented and tagged to the contract.

Revenue cutover & close activities (monthly)
- Finance generates revenue schedules and reconciles invoiced amounts to AR and deferred revenue ledger on the 3rd business day following month close.
- Any significant contract modifications (change orders > 10% of contract value) require re-assessment of revenue allocation.

Billing disputes & collections
- Customer disputes: Sales Ops logs dispute within billing system; Finance holds debit/credit memos pending resolution.
- Collections SLA: first past due contact at 7 days, escalation to manager at 30 days, involve Legal/Collections for > 60 days past due.

Accounting controls & documentation
- All invoices must reference contract ID and PO (if applicable).
- Supporting documentation for revenue recognition (SOW, acceptance criteria, delivery evidence) must be retained for audit (7 years retention).

Operational checklists & templates (quick reference)

Monthly close checklist (Finance)
- Reconcile bank accounts and merchant processor settlements.
- Reconcile deferred revenue to subscription system.
- Review AR aging and apply write-offs per policy.
- Produce revenue and margin variance analysis for leadership.

Procurement request template (required fields)
- Requester name, department, budget code, vendor name, estimated spend, justification, delivery timeline, contract attachment (if any).

Contract review checklist (Legal)
- Counterparty identity and authority.
- Term and termination rights.
- Payment terms and refund clauses.
- IP & data protection clauses.
- Limitation of liability and indemnities.
- Export control and sanctions screening.

Service level objectives (operational)
- Budget submission completeness: 95% of departmental budgets submitted by initial deadline.
- Standard PO issuance SLA: 90% within 3 business days.
- Contract triage turnaround: 80% of standard NDAs reviewed in 3 business days; 90% of standard contracts in 10 business days.

Exceptions & risk handling

- Exceptions to approval thresholds or contract terms require documented risk acceptance and sign-off by Legal and Finance (recorded in the Risk & Exceptions ledger).
- High-risk vendors (data processing, access to sensitive IP) require additional controls: SOC 2 report, data processing addendum, and restricted network access.

Related resources & attachments
- Budget template: /confluence/finance-and-legal/templates/budget-template-2026
- Contract intake form: /confluence/finance-and-legal/contracts-and-legal-process/contract-intake-form
- Vendor onboarding checklist: /confluence/finance-and-legal/procurement/vendor-onboarding-checklist
- Revenue recognition policy (authoritative): /confluence/finance-and-legal/revrec-and-billing/revenue-recognition-billing-policy-2026.json

Change history & governance
- This playbook is owned by Finance (Priya Nair). Major policy changes require Legal review and Exec sign-off.
- Review cadence: annual policy review and as-needed updates when accounting guidance or regulation changes.

Frequently asked questions (FAQ)
- Q: Who approves non-standard payment terms?
  A: Finance + Legal must approve any changes to standard payment terms; deviations documented on contract.
- Q: What if a vendor refuses standard contract terms?
  A: Escalate to Legal for negotiation; if material, route to the appropriate executive for approval per Signature Authority Matrix.

Appendix: Quick decision checklist (ordering)
- Is there an existing contract or SOW? If yes, reference contract ID.
- Is the spend within budget and below approval threshold? If yes, raise PR.
- Does the contract include data or export-sensitive clauses? If yes, include Legal in initial intake.

Contact & escalation
- Finance (general): finance@redwood.example
- Procurement / Vendor Ops: vendor-ops@redwood.example
- Legal (general counsel): legal@redwood.example

End of playbook.
